title: The verdict log attributes an agent's keep to the human who applied it
body:
## Summary
verdictLog.ts apply() writes the log line's `by` from the patch, not from the record, so a record stored by:'model' is logged by:'human'.

## Description
lib/foundry/verdictLog.ts:172 sets `who = by ?? "human"` from the PATCH's `by`, while store.ts verdictSpec.clean (lib/foundry/store.ts:164) keeps the RECORD's own `by` when it says human or model. The Board's forge apply (lib/decision/v1/sources/forge.ts:391) patches every decision with by:'human', and recordOf (forge.ts:156) writes an agent's decision as by:'model'. So the durable history (`verdicts.log.jsonl`, which the header calls the gate's history that outlives the media) says a human decided what the map says a model decided. Registry hitl-approval/decision-records: the `who` field is the authenticated decider. Which is right - the human who applied the packet, or the agent that cast the verdict - is a semantic call; the defect is that the two files disagree. Fix candidate: log `value.by` when the record carries one, else the patch's.

## Flow
- Board apply of a packet holding an agent decision -> patchVerdicts({set:{X:{verdict:'keep', by:'model'}}, by:'human'})
- verdicts.json X.by = model; verdicts.log.jsonl line by = human

## Expected impact
An audit of who kept what reads the log and over-counts human verdicts. Could break: a reader that relies on log.by meaning 'who pressed' (none in lib/: lib/ledger/v1/sources/forge.ts:34 says no reader exists).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the log's `by` equals the record's `by` on every set line
Before: simulation: 1 of 2 attributions disagree on the Board apply path for an agent decision (walked from forge.ts:156 and :391 through verdictLog.ts:172)
After: predicted 0 of 2
Method: simulation - no probe drives the Board apply with an agent decision in this round; the instrument is a case in foundry-verdict-patch.probe.spec.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/foundry/verdictLog.ts:172 `const who: VerdictBy = by ?? "human";`
lib/foundry/store.ts:164 `const who = rec.by === "human" || rec.by === "model" ? rec.by : by;`
lib/decision/v1/sources/forge.ts:156 `by: v1By(d.by)`; :391 `patchVerdicts(id, { ..., by: "human", surface: "board" })`
instrument: foundry-verdict-patch case: patchVerdicts with by:'human' and a set record by:'model' -> the log line's by equals the stored record's by

title: commitRun's auto-rejects bypass the verdict log and revision
body:
## Summary
With undecidedAs 'reject', commitRun writes the auto-rejected verdicts straight into verdicts.json, so the log and verdicts.rev.json never see them.

## Description
lib/foundry/store.ts commitRun adds `{verdict:'reject', at}` for every undecided candidate (the `undecidedAs === "reject"` block) and writes verdicts.json with fs.writeJsonAtomic near the end, outside the verdict kernel (lib/foundry/verdictLog.ts), whose header promises one log line per CHANGED key and a revision bump. commitExtractRun already goes through replaceVerdictMapHeld for its inline verdicts. No production caller passes 'reject' today (the Board's COMMIT_MODE is 'leave', lib/decision/v1/sources/forge.ts:85); the default parameter is 'reject', so the next caller that omits it inherits the gap.

## Flow
- commitRun(id) with the default undecidedAs
- verdicts.json gains N rejects; verdicts.log.jsonl gains 0 lines; verdicts.rev.json unchanged

## Expected impact
The gate's history misses the decisions that deleted files. Could break: the crash probe's effect count (foundry-commit-crash enumerates K mutations) moves by the log append and the rev write.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every verdict that deletes a file has a log line
Before: 0 of N auto-rejects logged (read from store.ts; N=1 in the crash probe's fixture, sc2)
After: N of N via replaceVerdictMapHeld(verdictSpec(id), run, verdicts, 'commit')
Method: simulation - the fix changes the crash probe's K and its prefix invariants, which needs its own isolated gate run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/foundry/store.ts: `if (undecidedAs === "reject") { for (const c of withFile) if (!verdicts[c.id]) verdicts[c.id] = { verdict: "reject", at }; }` ... `await fs.writeJsonAtomic(path.join(dir, "verdicts.json"), verdicts);`
lib/decision/v1/sources/forge.ts:85 `const COMMIT_MODE = "leave" as const;`
instrument: foundry-commit-crash fixture (sc2 undecided, 'reject'): count verdicts.log.jsonl set lines after commit == auto-rejected keys; then re-run the K-prefix enumeration green

title: The verdict-log append bypasses the fs port the crash probes stand on
body:
## Summary
fsPort.ts says every disk effect of the three commits goes through the port; verdictLog.ts appends verdicts.log.jsonl with node:fs appendFile directly, so a commit that takes inline verdicts has an effect no crash probe can kill at.

## Description
lib/foundry/fsPort.ts:1-20 (header) states the port carries every disk effect of commitRun, commitExtractRun and commitCycle. lib/foundry/verdictLog.ts apply() calls `appendFile` from node:fs/promises (the import on line 29), and commitExtractRun calls replaceVerdictMapHeld (lib/foundry/extract/store.ts) inside its commit. The RecordingPort (tests/golden-path/_effects.ts) therefore never sees the log append and cannot enumerate a crash between the log line and the map write - the very ordering apply()'s comment argues for ('the log leads'). Fix: an `appendFile` on FsPort, realFsPort delegating, RecordingPort recording it.

## Flow
- commitExtractRun with inline verdicts under the RecordingPort
- port.log has no entry for verdicts.log.jsonl

## Expected impact
The 'log leads the map' claim gets a probe. Could break: K in the extract crash enumeration grows by one; RecordingPort (a test file) must implement the new method.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - commit disk effects visible to the port: N-1 of N -> N of N
Before: the log append is 1 effect outside the port (read: verdictLog.ts imports appendFile from node:fs/promises)
After: 0 outside
Method: simulation - the port interface change touches tests/golden-path/_effects.ts and the extract crash probes, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/foundry/verdictLog.ts:29 `import { appendFile, stat } from "node:fs/promises";` and apply(): `await appendFile(path.join(spec.dir, VERDICT_LOG), ...)`
lib/foundry/fsPort.ts header: 'Every disk effect the three foundry COMMITS make ... goes through this one object'
instrument: RecordingPort log of commitExtractRun with inline verdicts contains the verdicts.log.jsonl append; a CrashAt between the append and the map write leaves a log line and an unchanged map

title: commitRun re-derives the plan it just computed, three rules twice
body:
## Summary
commitRun calls planForgeCommit for the token, then recomputes withFile, the undecided auto-reject and the ledger rows by hand; preview and commit already disagree on the rows' `at`.

## Description
lib/foundry/commitPlan.ts planForgeCommit builds withFile (status/deleted filter), the effective verdicts and ledgerRows; lib/foundry/store.ts commitRun repeats the same filter, the same auto-reject and its own ledger-row builder. Preview rows carry the verdict's `at`, committed rows the commit's `at` - a visible divergence in the Board's consequence vs ledger.json. The commitPlan header promises 'preview equals commit'. Fix: commitRun consumes plan.ledgerRows (stamped with the commit time) and plan.counts.

## Flow
- previewCommit(id).ledgerRows[i].at === verdict.at
- commitRun(id) writes ledger row at === commit time

## Expected impact
One rule site instead of two for what a commit deletes and records. Could break: the crash probe's convergence (the retry must write the same bytes).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - duplicated rule sites 3 -> 0
Before: 3 duplicated rules (withFile filter, auto-reject, ledger row builder) at store.ts and commitPlan.ts
After: 0
Method: probe - counted by reading both functions; the build is M and must re-run the crash-prefix enumeration in isolation
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/foundry/commitPlan.ts:48-90 (withFile, effectiveVerdicts, ledgerRows with `at: effectiveVerdicts[c.id].at || ""`)
lib/foundry/store.ts commitRun: `const withFile = run.candidates.filter(...)`, the auto-reject loop, and `ledger.rows.push({ ..., at, ...graderStamp(c.grade) })`
instrument: foundry-commit-plan Case 1 extended: plan.ledgerRows (minus `at`) deep-equals the rows commitRun writes; foundry-commit-crash K-prefix convergence stays green

title: grader-calibration.json is written in place, not atomically, inside the commit
body:
## Summary
commitRun writes the derived grader-calibration.json with fs.writeFile, the only tracked index in the commit not written by rename.

## Description
lib/foundry/store.ts commitRun: `await fs.writeFile(foundryFile("grader-calibration.json"), graderCalibrationText(...))`, beside writeJsonAtomic for ledger.json, verdicts.json and run.json. A crash mid-write leaves a torn file the Board's forge source reads (lib/decision/v1/sources/forge.ts reads the file as GraderCalibrationFile). The comment covers a STALE file (the retry rewrites it), not a TORN one. Fix: write via a text-atomic port method (or writeJsonAtomic of the object, if the trailing newline/format is kept byte-identical with calibrate.mts).

## Flow
- commitRun crashes during the calibration write
- pipeline/foundry/grader-calibration.json is half-written
- the Board's forge packet read of it fails until the next commit

## Expected impact
A crash cannot leave a torn tracked file. Could break: byte identity with pipeline/foundry/calibrate.mts output (foundry-calibration case 'tracked file is the calibration of the ledger').

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - torn-file windows on tracked indices 1 -> 0
Before: 1 of 4 commit-written tracked/run files non-atomic
After: 0 of 4
Method: simulation - a torn write is not producible through the RecordingPort without a partial-write mode
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a RecordingPort partial-write mode at the calibration write, then a Board forge read of the file: refuses today, reads the old file after
drain_note: needs a text-atomic FsPort method; honest size M

title: seedProofs swallows a plate read that throws, with no count of it
body:
## Summary
adopt.ts seedProofs skips a plate whose sidecar or PNG read THROWS with a bare catch, and proofsLeftOut counts only cap-excluded plates.

## Description
lib/foundry/adopt.ts seedProofs: `try { ... } catch { continue; }`. A null read (file absent) and a throw (EACCES, a damaged sidecar the reader rejects) both vanish; the draft's proofsLeftOut reports only SEED_CAP/SEED_BYTE_CAP exclusions, so an adoption that seeded 1 of 4 eligible plates because 3 failed to read says nothing. Fix: count read failures into a second leftOut reason, carrying the first error's message.

## Flow
- adoptInStore on a style with 4 kept text-lane plates, 3 unreadable
- draft.proofs.length 1, proofsLeftOut absent

## Expected impact
The operator sees why the sheet has fewer proofs. Could break: the AdoptionDraft shape consumers (lib/producers/style.ts) if a field is added rather than a reason.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - swallowed failure paths 1 -> 0
Before: 1 catch discards the error and its count
After: 0; the count rides in proofsLeftOut
Method: simulation - foundry-adopt.probe.spec.ts can inject a throwing readSidecar; not built this round (budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: foundry-adopt case: an AdoptIO whose readSidecar throws for 3 of 4 plates -> proofsLeftOut names 3 unreadable

title: Vestigial journal parameters: CatalogueTx.begin(ids) and withCatalogue(meta)
body:
## Summary
catalogue.ts begin(ids) and withCatalogue(meta) `void` their arguments since the journal retired; every commit still builds and passes them.

## Description
lib/foundry/catalogue.ts: `begin(ids: string[]) { void ids; ... }` and `withCatalogue(meta, fn) { void meta; ... }`. The callers (store.ts commitRun `tx.begin([...new Set(decided.map(...))])`, extract/training/strips stores) compute a style-id set and an op/run meta nobody reads. CatalogueTx.stamp() is likewise an empty method kept for two callers.

## Flow
- grep `void ids`, `void meta`, `async stamp(): Promise<void> {}` in lib/foundry/catalogue.ts

## Expected impact
Three dead parameters/methods and their caller-side computation go. Could break: nothing at runtime; four stores' call sites change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - vestigial parameters/methods 3 -> 0
Before: 3 (begin ids, withCatalogue meta, stamp)
After: 0
Method: probe - counted by grep; the callers are in extract/training/strips stores, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/foundry/catalogue.ts: `void ids;` in begin, `void meta;` in withCatalogue, `async stamp(): Promise<void> {}`
